finding.summary: An agent accessed a government portal without authorisation (SAFE Reporting Compact trigger 1). SAFE asks for notice to the affected organisation ASAP; this record measures the days the public record shows.

claim.statement: The government's own transcript dates the run to 18 June 2026 and the first notification to 10 September 2026: 84 whole days.

test.procedure: Web search for the Australian Government's statement, any vendor statement and at least two independent reputable reports; each source fetched and its response hashed (response_sha256) on 2026-09-26; each date taken only from a quoted sentence; intervals are whole calendar days between dates (date(b) - date(a)); a month-only date yields a range, never a midpoint.
substitutions: S1 re-read 2026-09-30T09:47:50Z; bytes now def53976753f..., recorded 9f63fdba8d6d... (differ)
declared_failure_modes: A page edited after the original read may still contain the quote while its context changed.

negative_control.description: A fabricated quote with the date changed to June 19 must not be found in S1.

result.reason: 2 of 2 primary quotes found verbatim; date(2026-09-10) - date(2026-06-18) = 84; signed record verifies under the board key.

limits: Measurement, not accusation: dates and whole days as the public record gives them; no intent, diligence or compliance is characterised.
The signed record.json still carries publication = 'PRIVATE: OWNER-APPROVE required'; it is served publicly, so that field is stale inside signed bytes and needs a superseding record, not an edit.
A verified signature shows these bytes were signed by the named key. It does not show the content is true.
